related_questions.question: Do I have to test for COVID if I was exposed?
related_questions.snippet: You can develop COVID-19 for up to 10 days after exposure. If you develop symptoms of COVID-19, start isolation immediately and get tested as soon as you can. If you have no symptoms of COVID-19, get tested on day 6 after your last exposure. You should test even if you do not have symptoms.

related_questions.question: How long after exposure to COVID will you test positive?
related_questions.snippet: Depending on which COVID-19 variant you've been exposed to, you may test positive 3-5 days later. If you've been exposed to the virus but don't have any symptoms, wait for 5 days before you get tested. If you test too early and you do have COVID-19, you may falsely test negative.

text_blocks.snippet: If you have been exposed to someone with COVID-19, it is important to get tested to prevent the spread of the virus. Here are the recommended testing guidelines:

list.snippet: Immediately: if you have symptoms of COVID-19 (such as fever, cough, shortness of breath, fatigue)
5-6 days after exposure: if you do not have symptoms
Again 48 hours after a negative test: if you still do not have symptoms

list.title: PCR test:
list.snippet: This is the most accurate test for detecting COVID-19. It can be performed at a healthcare provider's office or testing center.

list.title: Rapid antigen test:
list.snippet: This is a faster but less accurate test than a PCR test. It can be done at home or at a testing center.
If your test is positive, isolate yourself at home for at least 5 days and follow CDC guidelines for quarantine.
If your test is negative, continue to monitor for symptoms and wear a mask in public settings until you are fully vaccinated and boosted.
If you are immunocompromised or live with someone who is, consult with your healthcare provider for specific testing recommendations.
Follow local public health guidelines for testing and isolation requirements.
Consider getting vaccinated and boosted to protect yourself from COVID-19.

key_moments.title: THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION ON THURSDAY UPDATED ITS COVID-19 GUIDANCE ON QUARANTINE AND TESTING.

INSTEAD, PEOPLE CAN MASK UP FOR 10 DAYS AND GET TESTED FIVE DAYS AFTER THEY ARE EXPOSED TO THE VIRUS. SOURCE: CDC
SINCE PEOPLE NO LONGER NEED TO QUARANTINE AFTER AN EXPOSURE, THE CDC ALSO ENDED THE TEST-TO-STAY APPROACH IN SCHOOLS. SOURCE: CDC
STUDENTS WHO WERE EXPOSED CAN CONTINUE IN-PERSON CLASSES IF THEY REMAIN ASYMPTOMATIC AND TEST NEGATIVE. SOURCE: CDC
PEOPLE WITH COVID CAN LEAVE ISOLATION AFTER TWO NEGATIVE TEST RESULTS BEFORE GOING IN PUBLIC AGAIN WITHOUT A MASK. SOURCE CDC
